![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/4eaf3eac9364aca72506f0d11c7d69332bbf853871d85986e45bd3082a607354.png)

Consider the region bounded by $y=1-{x}^{2}$ and $y={x}^{2}-2x+1,$ as shown above. Which of the following gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=1-{x}^{2}$ and $g(x)={x}^{2}-2x+1.$

First, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation for $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ 1-{x}^{2} & ={x}^{2}-2x+1 \\ 2{x}^{2}-2x & =0 \\ x(x-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=1.$

Let's draw our vertical arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing *away* from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/3fc8d26f99a0b640983b047af4e201fe5f8164c9d6ebc7f5bd234ae706fed796.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $y=g(x)={x}^{2}-2x+1,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $y=f(x)=1-{x}^{2}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({[1-{x}^{2}]}^{2}-{[{x}^{2}-2x+1]}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({[\text{ }1-{x}^{2}]}^{2}-{[1-x]}^{4})\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
